Rafael M.: Quick one  I moved my adult child (age 22) back from university in Spain and want to add them to my medical. They were previously covered by their school's plan abroad. Is that a QLE? What proof do you need for an international dependent?

Asha (People Ops): Congrats on the return! Short answer: yes, loss of other coverage is typically a QLE. For international dependents we need docs that carriers accept: termination of prior coverage, proof of residence, and dependency proof.

Rafael M.: I have a letter from the Spanish insurer showing they lost coverage (graduation/terminated), and a lease in my child's name in the US starting next month. Do carriers accept foreign insurer letters?

Max (Benefits Ops): Carriers accept foreign insurer letters but need translation + apostille/notarization in some cases. Useful bundle: termination letter (translated), passport or national ID, US lease or dorm contract, and proof of financial support or tax claim if available. If your child was on another employer plan, a certificate of prior coverage helps.

Rafael M.: My kid isn't claimed on my taxes yet. I do provide >50% support while they were abroad. What counts as proof of support?

Asha (People Ops): Acceptable support docs: joint bank transfers (3+ showing regular support), wire receipts, proof of paying tuition or rent, or a signed affidavit plus bank statements showing >50% support. Carriers vary so provide as much as you can. Redact full account numbers.

Rafael M.: Got it. Also timeline: the insurer letter lists termination date 2026-05-31. I uploaded the translated letter + lease + bank transfer screenshots to the portal (file: rafael_international_bundle_1976543225.pdf).

Benefits Bot: Upload received from Rafael M.  File ID: upload_1976543226  Status: awaiting review.

Max (Benefits Ops): Reviewing now. Two quick checks: 1) QLE window is 30 days from loss of coverage; you filed within that window so good. 2) For translation: if not translated by certified translator we may ask for notarized translation or apostille depending on carrier. I'll flag translation requirement in my review.

Compliance Bot: Reminder: do NOT include full SSNs in uploads. Acceptable redaction: last four digits only. Non-US IDs should be translated and notarized if requested by carrier.

Lina (Payroll): FYI payroll will need the effective date from Benefits to set deductions. If the carrier lets the effective date be the termination date (05/31/2026) and approves retro, we'll do a one-time catch-up adjustment. If effective date is first of next month after approval, deductions start thereafter. Expect 1 payroll cycle for the change to appear.

Rafael M.: Thanks. Any tip to speed carrier approval for international docs?

Max (Benefits Ops): Provide certified translation + apostille if available, include the insurer's official stamp, and a short cover note explaining the situation. I can submit a carrier cover letter highlighting the QLE & translation status to reduce back-and-forth.

Asha (People Ops): I'll follow up once Max confirms carrier submission. Rafael, I'll DM if anything is missing. :thumbsup:

Rafael M.: Appreciate it  uploaded certified translation as "rafael_translation_1976543238.pdf". Thanks team!
